title: Finnfund — CREI South Sudan solar-hybrid telecom energy follow-on, 2026
description: "Finnfund, a Finnish development financier, has committed a $5 million follow-on investment in Communication and Renewable Energy Infrastructure (CREI) to help South Sudan scale its sustainable telecom energy infrastructure." The funds are "backed by the European Fund for Sustainable Development Plus (EFSD+) as part of the Africa Connected programme"; Finnfund has invested US$10m in CREI in total. "Finnfund's finance will help MTN South Sudan's 499 telecom sites modernise and expand their solar-hybrid energy systems as part of a 10-year Energy-as-a-Service contract." The project has renovated 490 sites, served over four million people, and overall network coverage rose from 69% to 80% of the population over three years.

title: CREI South Sudan Telecom Energy Infrastructure
description: Finnfund USD 5 million mezzanine loan to CREI to finance installation, operation and maintenance of 413 solar-hybrid energy systems for MTN South Sudan telecom sites. The project expands mobile network coverage in South Sudan, one of the world's least connected countries, benefiting over 2 million people with reliable mobile and internet access.

title: Chinese Government provides $20 million grant for Phase 2 of Educational Technical Cooperation Project (Linked to Project ID#59201)
description: In March 2015, the Chinese Government and the Government of South Sudan agreed to conduct a feasibility study for the Educational Technical Cooperation Project. The feasibility study was completed in May 2015. Then, on February 3, 2016, the Chinese Government and the Government of South Sudan signed an exchange of letters regarding Phase 1 of the Educational Technical Cooperation Project. China’s Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) reportedly committed $6 million of grant funding for the project’s first phase (captured via Project ID#59201).   Phase 1 involved the design of courses, the training for over 200 South Sudanese teachers in China, the printing of over 1,299,000 textbooks for use by 150,000 teachers and students, and the construction of training centers. China South Publishing and Media Group (中南出版传媒集团股份有限公司) was the contractor responsible for project implementation. Phase 1 officially commenced on June 29, 2016. One month later, on July 29, 2016, MOFCOM awarded a contract to China South Publishing and Media Group. Then, on December 23, 2016, a project implementation agreement was signed by the Chinese Government and the Government of South Sudan. The first phase of teacher training activities was completed in April 2017. During Phase 1, 54 teachers were trained including 14 members of parliament who were members of the education committee. Then, on July 14, 2017, the first batch of 745,000 textbooks and the equipment of the ICT teacher training center arrived in Juba. The second batch of 554,000 textbooks was scheduled for printing by the end of 2017. The project’s first phase passed a mid-term inspection by MOFCOM in December 2017. A one-month ICT training was successfully completed in South Sudan in February 2018. The project’s ICT infrastructure and ICT training component was completed in September 2018. title: China Eximbank provides $248.8 million loan for Air Traffic Management System (ATMS) Project
description: On January 25, 2018, the Chinese Ambassador to South Sudan and the South Sudanese Finance Minister signed a preferential loan framework agreement. On the same day, the Government of South Sudan and China Eximbank signed a $248.8 million loan agreement for the Air Traffic Management System (ATMS) Project. The borrowing terms of the loan are unknown. However, it is known the borrower was expected to use the proceeds of the loan to finance a commercial (EPC) contract between South Sudan Civil Aviation Authority and China Harbor Engineering Company (CHEC) Limited, which was signed on October 14, 2016. This loan is reportedly secured by (collateralized against) airport fees/revenues that the borrower is required to deposit in a lender-controlled escrow account.  The loan's amount outstanding was $231,952,567 as of December 2022.  The purpose of the project is to construct Juba ATMS center, a new Air Traffic control tower and operation building, a surveillance system, a navigation system, and a communication system. The Juba ATMS center is located next to Juba International Airport. The project also involves the civil engineering and supporting facilities required by the equipment (such as meteorological facilities), calibration flight test training, and other forms of training for South Sudanese technicians (to prepare them for management of the air space by 2023).   CHEC is the EPC contractor responsible for implementation. Project implementation commenced in June 2020 and it was originally expected to reach completion by June 2023. On July 6, 2021, South Sudan Civil Aviation Authority (SSCAA) announced the launch of a state-of-the-art online system, which allows the opening of new routes. The newly established lower airspace, launched in partnership with aviation solutions provider NavPass, is designed to boost tourism and generate revenue for the economy, according to SSCAA.
